federalIncidentCoordinator: Dana Whitfield, VP of Compliance, dana.whitfield@meridianfed.com, 202-555-0142
incidentDescription: Automated monitoring detected a burst of failed login attempts against the tenant-facing authentication endpoint originating from a small set of IP addresses, consistent with a credential-stuffing attempt using a previously breached password list. The endpoint's rate limiting and account lockout controls contained the activity before any account was compromised.

timeline.detectionSource: SIEM correlation rule: anomalous failed-login velocity by source IP

milestones.milestoneDescription: SIEM alert fired and paged the on-call security engineer.
Source IPs added to the WAF blocklist; automated account lockouts confirmed active.
Incident evaluated against FedRAMP reportability criteria; determined reportable as a precaution given volume of affected accounts targeted.
Activity ceased; no successful authentications from the source IPs confirmed via log review.

potentialImpact: Low potential impact. No account compromise occurred and no CUI was accessed; impact assessment based on the volume of accounts targeted rather than any confirmed data exposure.
functionalImpact: No functional impact to the service. The affected authentication endpoint remained available throughout, and no legitimate user sessions were disrupted.
recoveryPlan: No recovery actions were required beyond the automated containment already performed (IP blocklisting, account lockouts). The reduced lockout threshold change was deployed within 48 hours as a preventative hardening measure.
observedActivity: Approximately 1,400 failed login attempts across 340 distinct tenant accounts within a 3-minute window, originating from 6 source IP addresses in a single /24 block. Password attempts matched patterns consistent with a known public credential-stuffing list.
indicatorsOfCompromise: User-Agent string: "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; okhttp/4.9.0)" used consistently across all attempts
rootCause: Credential-stuffing attack using a third-party breached-password list; not a vulnerability in MOCP's own systems.
responseAndRecoveryActivities: Source IPs were blocklisted at the WAF within 6 minutes of detection. Automated account lockout policy (already in place) prevented any successful authentication. Post-incident, the failed-login threshold was tightened from 10 to 5 attempts within a 5-minute window, and affected tenant administrators were notified out of an abundance of caution.
